context.brief:
## Employee
- Name: Test User (no id)
- Role: Plant Manager, HSE
- Plant / unit: Tokyo / Unit 300

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Plant Manager's undocumented decision-making heuristics
topics.rationale: Capture the unwritten rules and mental models used to prioritize conflicting demands, especially balancing production, safety, and maintenance.
seed_questions: When you had conflicting priorities, what unwritten rules guided your decisions?
Can you walk me through a recent crisis where you had to make a call without all the data?
What early indicators do you watch that aren't on any dashboard?

topics.title: HSE leadership and safety culture nuances
topics.rationale: Understand how safety culture was actually built and sustained beyond formal policies, including buy-in tactics and informal enforcement.
seed_questions: What safety practices did you implement that aren't in the official HSE manual?
How did you get buy-in from operators for new safety initiatives?
Are there unwritten safety norms that you fear will fade after you leave?

topics.title: Unfinished or shelved improvement projects
topics.rationale: Identify projects that were started but not completed, their current state, obstacles, and who holds critical knowledge to restart them.
seed_questions: Are there any improvement projects you initiated that are still in limbo? What's the current state?
What were the key obstacles, and who holds the institutional knowledge to restart them?
Which shelved project would you revive first if you had the resources?

topics.title: Lessons learned from past HSE incidents
topics.rationale: Uncover root causes and corrective actions that were not fully captured in official reports, including early warning signs.
seed_questions: Can you recall a significant HSE incident where the official report didn't capture the full story?
What were the early warning signs that were missed?
What informal changes were made afterward that aren't documented?

topics.title: Critical equipment list and their hidden failure modes
topics.rationale: Since no equipment is recorded, ask the manager to name the most critical assets in Unit 300 and share undocumented failure patterns and workarounds.
seed_questions: Which equipment in Unit 300 keeps you up at night? What are the failure modes that aren't in the manuals?
Are there any pumps, compressors, or vessels that have recurring issues with undocumented workarounds?
What early-warning signs do you personally look for during walkthroughs?

topics.title: Vendor and contractor relationships for key equipment
topics.rationale: Capture who to call, vendor quirks, and support quality that isn't written in contracts or service agreements.
seed_questions: For the critical equipment you mentioned, which vendors or contractors have the best troubleshooting knowledge?
Are there specific people we should maintain relationships with?
What are the unwritten rules for dealing with vendor support to get faster or better service?

topics.title: Tribal knowledge: unwritten rules and gotchas in Unit 300
topics.rationale: Document the informal knowledge that everyone on the floor knows but is never written down, preventing future incidents.
seed_questions: What are the unwritten rules that every new operator in Unit 300 needs to know?
Can you share a 'gotcha' that caused a problem because someone didn't know the tribal knowledge?
Which piece of equipment has a 'personality' that only experienced operators understand?

topics.title: Informal communication networks and key influencers
topics.rationale: Map the real information flow and go-to people beyond the organizational chart, especially during emergencies.
seed_questions: Who are the go-to people for specific issues that aren't in their job descriptions?
How does information really flow in the plant, especially during emergencies?
Who are the informal leaders that you rely on to get things done?

topics.title: Procedural shortcuts and workarounds that are safe but undocumented
topics.rationale: Identify where standard operating procedures are routinely bypassed with safer or more efficient informal methods.
seed_questions: Are there any standard procedures that are routinely done differently because the official way is impractical?
How do you ensure safety when these workarounds are used?
What workarounds have you personally approved that aren't written down?

topics.title: Emergency response procedures: gaps and real-world execution
topics.rationale: Reveal where written emergency plans fail in practice and what ad-hoc actions were taken during real incidents.
seed_questions: During a real emergency, what parts of the written emergency plan fell apart? What did you do instead?
Are there any emergency scenarios that aren't covered in the current plans?
What drill feedback never made it into the official revisions?

topics.title: Successor advice: open risks and priority actions
topics.rationale: Provide the incoming manager with a candid list of hidden risks and immediate focus areas not found in formal reports.
seed_questions: If you had to give your successor one piece of advice that isn't in any report, what would it be?
What are the top three risks you see that are not being actively managed right now?
Which relationships or political dynamics should they be aware of from day one?

topics.title: Regulatory and compliance nuances
topics.rationale: Capture informal strategies for managing audits, regulators, and compliance gaps that are handled outside official processes.
seed_questions: How do you prepare for regulatory audits beyond the official checklist? What are the common pitfalls?
Are there any compliance issues that you've managed informally that could become problems later?
What unwritten rules do you follow when interacting with specific regulators?

topics.title: Capital project justifications and political landscape
topics.rationale: Understand how projects were truly justified and approved, including internal politics and rejected but necessary initiatives.
seed_questions: What were the most challenging capital projects to get approved, and how did you navigate the internal politics?
Are there any projects that were rejected but you still believe are necessary?
Who were the key allies or blockers in the approval process?

topics.title: Maintenance strategies and reliability secrets
topics.rationale: Uncover undocumented condition monitoring tricks, maintenance interval adjustments, and reliability insights for critical assets.
seed_questions: For the critical equipment, what condition monitoring indicators do you rely on that aren't in the official maintenance plan?
Are there any maintenance tasks that are done more or less frequently than the manual says, and why?
What reliability 'hacks' have you learned from experience that aren't shared widely?

topics.title: Historical incidents and near-misses that shaped current practices
topics.rationale: Capture stories of past incidents or near-misses that are not formally recorded but heavily influence current behavior and unwritten rules.
seed_questions: Can you tell me about a near-miss that changed how you operate but was never officially documented?
What incident from the past do you think new people should know about to understand why we do things a certain way?
Are there any 'ghost stories' that operators tell that actually contain important lessons?

transcript.text: Hello Test User. Thank you for sitting down with me today. I know retirement is right around the corner, and the truth is, there's a whole lot of knowledge in your head that lives nowhere else — so before you walk out the door, I want to make sure we capture what matters most for the person stepping into your shoes.
